findings.reason: the clause must be per-node ("the guard passes with this module no longer in the allowlist", leaving the empty-allowlist condition to the section/merge level), or §7 must be dispatched as one node over all three moves; otherwise a dispatched §7 node holds an unsatisfiable measure and its gate proves nothing.
findings.text: §7 says each of mcp.py, runs.py, _backends.py "is one node", but its single done-when requires "the guard passes with the module removed from its allowlist and the allowlist then empty": the allowlist can be empty only once every oversize module has been split, so a node that has split just mcp.py cannot satisfy "then empty", and creating an empty allowlist while runs.py and _backends.py (§7) plus recovery.py (§5) and promotion.py (§6) are still over the 50,000 bound turns the guard red because §2 fails any file above the bound that is not allowlisted — the clause is satisfiable only after all of §3–§7 have landed, never by one §7 node

findings.reason: the under-count does not change the bound choice (a larger count strengthens 50,000 over 40,000), it only misstates the support for it.
findings.text: the rationale says a 40,000 bound would force "four more modules (the ledger, the server, routing and budget, all between 41,000 and 44,000)" to be split, but five files exceed 40,000 estimated tokens today: tests/test_crew.py 49,747, ledger 43,523, routing 43,119, serve 43,374, budget 41,496 — the largest, tests/test_crew.py at just under the chosen 50,000 bound, is omitted, and the guard measures `tests/` too
